verdict.rationale: Both changes make identical source edits: the same event type, the same `paused` status and nullable `resumeOn`, the same reducer guards, and the same audit and notifier cases. All of these match the spec, including clearing `resumeOn` on cancel and leaving a paused subscription alone on payment events. The tests cover the same cases. A checks the initial null `resumeOn` in its own test, while B folds that check into the pause test. Both reports are accurate about what changed and their test counts (20 and 19) match their diffs, so I would be equally happy merging either.

The production code in both changes is identical and correct: new event type, `paused` status, `resumeOn` field, payment no-ops while paused, cancel clears `resumeOn`, audit line and notification. The tests cover the same behaviors, and the reported test counts (19 vs 20) are accurate. B splits the initial-null check into its own test, and its report warns that a paused subscription currently has no way back to active. That caveat is useful for the developer and tips this slightly to B.
